en: A single large cumulus cloud can weigh over one million pounds, making it surprisingly heavy despite being made of tiny water droplets.
The Atacama Desert in Chile is considered the driest non-polar place on Earth, with some weather stations never recording any rainfall.
A single teaspoon of healthy forest soil contains more living microorganisms than the total number of people currently on Earth.
Pumice is the only natural rock that floats on water because it is formed from frothy, gas-filled volcanic lava.
The mineral fluorite glows brightly under ultraviolet light, displaying a fascinating property known as fluorescence.
A single large oak tree can absorb and release up to 400 liters of water into the air every single day through transpiration.
A single day on Venus lasts longer than its entire year because the planet rotates on its axis extremely slowly.
Saturn is the only planet in our solar system that is less dense than water, meaning it would theoretically float in a giant bathtub.
Neutron stars are incredibly dense, meaning a single teaspoon of their material would weigh about six billion tons on Earth.
Footprints left by Apollo astronauts on the lunar surface will remain perfectly preserved for millions of years due to the lack of wind.
In the deep ocean, a tsunami wave can travel at the speed of a commercial jet, exceeding 800 kilometers per hour.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines injected so much ash into the atmosphere that it temporarily cooled global temperatures.
